document:
# Using Retrieval Augmented Generation > Using Retrieval Augmented Generation

Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) in Data 360 is a framework for grounding large
    language model (LLM) prompts. By augmenting the prompt with accurate, current, and pertinent
    information, RAG improves the relevance and value of LLM responses for users.

When you submit an LLM prompt, RAG in Data 360:

- Retrieves relevant information from structured and unstructured data indexed in Data
        Cloud’s vector database
- Augments the prompt by combining this information with the original prompt
- Generates a prompt response

It’s helpful to think of RAG in two main parts: offline preparation and online usage.

metadata.breadcrumb: Using Retrieval Augmented Generation > Using Retrieval Augmented Generation

document:
# Using Retrieval Augmented Generation > Offline Preparation (Part 1)

To implement RAG, start by connecting structured and
      unstructured data that RAG uses to ground LLM prompts.

Data 360 uses a vector database to
        manage unstructured data. The vector database contains a collection of structured and
        unstructured content (a search index) that is indexed in a search-optimized way. Content can
        be ingested from a variety of sources and file types. Some examples of unstructured content
        used with RAG include service replies, cases, RFP responses, knowledge articles, emails, and
        meeting notes.

Offline preparation involves these steps:

- Connect your unstructured data.
- Create a search index configuration to chunk and vectorize the content. Chunking
            breaks the text into smaller, semantically meaningful units, and vectorization converts
            chunks into numeric representations of the text that capture semantic
          similarities.

Chunking
            breaks the text into smaller, semantically meaningful units, and vectorization converts
            chunks into numeric representations of the text that capture semantic
          similarities.

metadata.breadcrumb: Using Retrieval Augmented Generation > Offline Preparation (Part 1)

document:
# Using Retrieval Augmented Generation > Offline Preparation (Part 2)

- Store and manage the search index in Data 360. Retrievers serve as the bridge
            between search indexes and prompt templates. Retrievers further refine the search
            criteria and retrieve the most relevant information used to augment prompts. To support
            a variety of use cases, you create custom retrievers in AI Models (formerly Einstein Studio). To learn more,
            see Retrieve Data .

Retrievers serve as the bridge
            between search indexes and prompt templates. Retrievers further refine the search
            criteria and retrieve the most relevant information used to augment prompts. To support
            a variety of use cases, you create custom retrievers in AI Models (formerly Einstein Studio). To learn more,
            see Retrieve Data .

metadata.breadcrumb: Using Retrieval Augmented Generation > Offline Preparation (Part 2)

document:
# Using Retrieval Augmented Generation > Online Usage

The final piece of the RAG implementation is to call a
      retriever in a prompt template. For a given prompt template, the prompt designer can customize
      retriever query and result settings to populate a prompt with the most relevant
        information.

Online usage involves these steps:

- The retriever is invoked with a dynamic query initiated from the prompt template.
- The query is vectorized (converted to numeric representations). Vectorization enables
          search to find semantic matches in the search index.
- The query retrieves the relevant context from Data 360’s vector database.
- The original prompt is populated with the information retrieved from the search
          index.
- The prompt is submitted to the LLM, which generates and returns the prompt response.

Many LLMs were trained generally across the Internet on older content. With RAG,
        prompt template users can provide the LLM with the most accurate, up-to-date information, as
        well as bring proprietary data to the LLM without retraining and fine-tuning the model,
        creating generated responses that are more pertinent to their context and use case.

metadata.breadcrumb: Using Retrieval Augmented Generation > Online Usage

# Connect Data > Connect Data

To get started with Data 360 , you connect a data source, through
    either data federation or data ingestion. Data federation sets up direct connectivity with data
    sources. It uses a zero copy integration that eliminates the need to ingest data into Data 360 . During data ingestion, data is brought into Data 360 in its original form and stored in a data lake object (DLO).

As of October 14, 2025, Data Cloud has been rebranded to Data 360. During this
          transition, you may see references to Data Cloud in our application and documentation.
          While the name is new, the functionality and content remains unchanged.

metadata.breadcrumb: Connect Data > Connect Data

document:
# Connect Data > Connectors

You can connect data sources, such as Amazon S3, Marketing Cloud Engagement, and Google
        Storage, to Data 360 using a dedicated connector. Select the data source
        connector that you want to import data from, and then indicate the objects or dataset that
        you want to connect. Data 360 retrieves a sample of your data and provides
        a recommended source schema for your review. Find detailed integration and connector
        documentation in the Data Cloud Integration Guide .

metadata.breadcrumb: Connect Data > Connectors

document:
# Connect Data > Data Streams

A data stream uses a connector to establish a connection with a data source. A data stream
        acts as a pipeline for connecting data to Data 360 . The ingested data is
        organized into a schema and stored as data lake objects (DLOs).

When creating a data stream, you specify the category and optionally the event time,
        primary key, and organization unit identifier. You can enhance your data using formula
        fields to clean and adjust raw data. You can also configure the scheduling details to manage
        how often data is refreshed.

- Data Object Concepts and Schema in Data 360 During ingestion, Data 360 retrieves a sample of your data and     recommends a source schema. You can then review and modify the recommended schema.
- Data Sources in Data 360 Data sources are ingested into or connected to Data 360 in different     ways with specific requirements and steps that an admin configures before creating a data     stream.
- Data Streams in Data 360 Data streams are the connections and associated data ingested into Data 360 .

document:
# Use Search for AI, Automation, and Analytics > Vector Search

In Data 360 , you can create searchable vector embeddings from your
        unstructured and structured data. A vector embedding is a numerical representation of a unit
        of text (an article or a passage from a larger document) that captures its semantic meaning.
        Large language models (LLMs) group embeddings with similar semantic meanings so that
        generative AI applications can effectively interpret their relationships and contextual
        relevance.

Use vector search when your data source and
        search queries benefit more from semantically aware matches within a large dataset. For
        example, if you send a query such as “What is Acme famous for?”, the LLM retrieves chunks
        that have the highest vector search score that relates to the closest semantic match with
        the search query.

Before you create a vector search index, unstructured data stored in data model objects (DMOs) or
        unstructured data model objects (UDMOs) are chunked into manageable, semantically meaningful
        units. These units are stored in two objects : a chunk data model object (CDMO) and an
        index data model object (IDMO). The CDMO is a Data 360 object that stores
        the actual content chunks, and the IDMO stores the vector embedding.

You can perform vector
        searches on that data from apps such as Prompt Builder, AI agents, or Tableau.

metadata.doc_title: Use Search for AI, Automation, and Analytics
metadata.breadcrumb: Use Search for AI, Automation, and Analytics > Vector Search

document:
# Use Search for AI, Automation, and Analytics > Hybrid Search

To deliver relevant and accurate responses in generative
        AI applications, Large Language Models (LLMs) often require both vector and keyword search.
        While vector search excels at grasping semantic similarities, it can lack precision with
        specific domain vocabulary. Conversely, keyword search is excellent for lexical matches but
        doesn't understand semantic similarity. In Data 360 , hybrid search combines these methods,
        using semantically aware vector search for contextual understanding and keyword search for
        precise lexical matching.

When your data source and search queries benefit from both
        semantically aware vector search and the precision of a keyword search, use hybrid search.
        For example, in the query “Does Acme motor XYZ123 use hydraulic pumps?” the addition of
        keyword search promotes higher-ranking positions for more relevant content, thus providing
        the results with better grounding.

After you create a hybrid search index on your DMOs or UDMOs, Data 360 generates content chunks and vector embeddings for a vector search index and a keyword
        search index. Hybrid search queries the vector search index to retrieve information based on
        semantic similarity, and it queries the keyword search index to retrieve information based
        on lexical similarity. Hybrid search then merges and ranks the results provided by both
        types of searches to generate the best response. You can also configure additional ranking
        factors, such as recency or popularity of records, to influence the search results
        returned.

- In Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG): Data 360 search is

- In Service Cloud: AI agents use search to query for precise information within knowledge
          articles, emails, support tickets, and chat logs. This enables them to provide more
          accurate answers, craft better responses, and even proactively suggest solutions to
          customer issues.
- In Sales Cloud: AI agents can query unstructured sales data—like emails, call
          transcripts, and notes—to generate highly relevant meeting briefings and summaries. This
          insight also fuels personalized content and customer-specific recommendations for new
          emails, significantly boosting customer engagement and sales team productivity.
- In automation flows: AI agents can automatically identify semantically similar records,
          such as Cases, based on their descriptions. This capability is crucial for flagging
          duplicates, accelerating resolution times, and accurately classifying records by finding
          similar historical examples.
- In analytics: Within Tableau, Data 360 search facilitates gaining
          deeper insights from unstructured data, notably through advanced topic classification.
          This enhances data analysis by revealing patterns and themes that traditional methods
          sometimes miss.
- Chunk Data To add your data to Data 360’s search index, you must first chunk it. Chunking break   your data into meaningful chunks, and Data 360 turns those chunks into machine-readable vector   embeddings.
- Vector Search In Data 360, you can create searchable semantic vector embeddings from your     unstructured and structured data. Vector search helps your generative AI, automation, and     analytics applications understand semantic similarities and context between     embeddings.
- Hybrid Search To provide relevant information to an LLM with gen AI applications and generate the   correct response, requires both vector search and keyword search. Vector search understands   semantic similarities and context, but lacks specific domain vocabulary. Keyword search excels at   lexical similarity but not at semantic similarity. In Data 360, hybrid search combines the   strengths of semantically aware vector search with the precision and speed of keyword   search.
- Manage Search Indexes Create, view, edit, and delete search index configurations.
- Optimizing Search Indexes: Field Selection and Chunking When you create a search index in the advanced builder, you can optimize your search     index to deliver more accurate results by paying attention to the field selection and chunking     strategies you use.

By augmenting the prompt with accurate, current, and pertinent     information, RAG improves the relevance and value of LLM responses for users.

# Unify Source Profiles > Unify Source Profiles (Part 1)

Use identity resolution in Data 360 to consolidate data from
    different sources into comprehensive views of your customers and accounts. Identity resolution
    uses matching and reconciliation rules to link data about people or accounts into unified
    profiles. Identity resolution creates complete, actionable views of your customers but doesn’t
    create golden records and isn’t a master data management (MDM) system. Each unified profile
    contains all the unique contact point values from all sources. You choose which view of your
    customers to use based on each business use case you want to solve.

As of October 14, 2025, Data Cloud has been rebranded to Data 360. During this
          transition, you may see references to Data Cloud in our application and documentation.
          While the name is new, the functionality and content remains unchanged.

Unified profile data empowers your reps to sell, service, and market more effectively with
      360-degree views of each customer.

- Prioritize high-value leads from existing or key accounts.
- Boost sales effectiveness with personalized, relevant marketing across channels.
- Enable seamless information sharing across departments.
- Equip reps with full account history for contextual conversations and cross-channel
        consistency.
- Empower sales and service to identify cross-sell and upsell opportunities.

- About Identity Resolution Identity resolution is the processing engine that generates unified profiles from     source profile data stored in Data 360. Unified profiles act as a system of reference to     unlock our source data. Understand how and when source profiles are processed and what you can     do with unified profile output.
- Profile Unification Types Identity resolution in Data 360 offers several different ways to unify your records.     The unification type you select determines what types of objects you can base your unified     profiles on, the output objects created by the ruleset, and the speed at which records can be     unified.

# Enrich Your Org with 360 Data and Insights > Required Editions (Part 1)

You can add information from Data 360 to your Salesforce CRM record pages using
        enrichments. There are three types of enrichments.

- Related Lists—Related lists show information for DMO objects. DMO objects have a
          1-to-many relationship to a Data 360 Individual or Unified Individual object. For example,
          a contact can have many email engagements. With a related list, you can see all of the
          email engagements across your enterprise for your contact.
- Direct-DMO Related Lists—Direct-DMO related lists show information from any DMO that's
          connected to the Salesforce object through a direct relationship. The direct relationship
          doesn't require identity resolution to be completed for the DMO. For example, a Vehicle
          object in Automotive Cloud can have a related list of Vehicle Telematics Event DMO records
          from Data 360.
- Copy Fields—Copy Fields show field data copied from objects with a 1-to-1 relationship
          to a Data 360 Individual, Unified Individual, Data 360 Account, or Unified Account DMO.
          CIO objects must have a single Individual ID as the dimension or be a multi-dimensional
          aggregatable CIO.

- Create a Direct-DMO Related List Enrichment Add information to a Salesforce object related list from a Data Cloud DMO by using a     direct relationship between the DMO and the Salesforce object. The direct relationship doesn't     require that you complete identity resolution for the DMO. For example, a Vehicle object in     Automotive Cloud can have a related list of Vehicle Telematics Event DMO records from Data     Cloud.

After you finish testing your enrichments, package them in a data kit and deploy it to production using change sets.
- Create a Copy Field Enrichment Add information from Data 360 data model objects (DMO) to record pages in your org, so     you can show information and interactions from multiple systems, orgs, or business units in a     related list.

To avoid returning data that isn’t relevant to the records in your org, the enrichment     matches data from your org to data in Data Cloud. How the data is matched determines what data     is returned.

# Ingest Google Analytics into Data Cloud > Configuration Considerations (Part 2)

- BigQuery Export is available only in Google Analytics 360.
- Data in Google Analytics BigQuery resides in the United States, by default. Therefore,
          Google Analytics BigQuery Export is incompatible with Google Cloud Platform (GCP) policies
          that prohibit the creation of datasets in the United States. To align with these policies,
          localize your dataset to the European Union.
- Don’t link more than 300 Google Analytics reporting views to a single BigQuery Project
          because doing so degrades the export of intradata trading.
- You can link only one Google Analytics reporting view to each property.
- After connecting your Google Analytics data to your BigQuery project, Analytics data
          appears within 24 hours. Each day, the previous day’s data is exported as a single file,
          and the current day’s data is exported as three.
- You can link only one Google Analytics reporting view to each property.
- The service account must have EDIT access to your BigQuery project to turn on data
          exporting.

# Ingest Google Analytics into Data Cloud > Configuration Considerations (Part 3)

- Salesforce data integrated using the measurement protocol is stored in Google Analytics
          as custom dimensions.
- Google Analytics generates client IDs.
- Google Analytics only tracks events associated with a user ID.
- Google Analytics tracks only events associated with a user ID. Unassociated events are
          discarded from the user ID profile.
- If a visitor signs in or registers during a session, events before the authentication
          are associated with the user ID.
- When using the measurement protocol with your own visitor identifier (UID), your Google
          Analytics view is split: one profile shows all your website traffic without insights on
          cross-device activity, and the other shows only user ID traffic with cross-device insight.
- If you can’t assign an ID to a user, don’t send the uid parameter. All users without the
          necessary data still count against your data limits and can cause reporting discrepancies.
- For Marketing Cloud Engagement customers, you can use the Subscriber ID (sfmc_id) as the
          uid for tracking. To pass the sfmc_id query parameter to the uid field in the Google
          Analytics tag, set up a Custom Dimension in Google Analytics and modify the Google

Learn how to set up and use audience activations from Data Cloud to power an
    omnichannel journey in Marketing Cloud Engagement. This guide walks you through an example of

This solution kit makes these assumptions. You’re creating an omnichannel journey in
      Marketing Cloud Engagement that contains email, SMS, and MobilePush channels. Your
      organization has implemented single-channel contacts for Engagement for all three channels but

# Create Omnichannel Journeys Using Unified Individual Profiles in Data Cloud > Related Content (Part 2)

- Associated Terms for Omnichannel Journeys Using Data 360 Review terms that you must know when creating your data foundation.
- Model Your Contact Data for Omnichannel Journeys This solution kit is designed for customers who have implemented single-channel contacts   in Marketing Cloud Engagement. Customers who have implemented single-channel contacts in Marketing   Cloud Engagement must follow this solution kit to execute omnichannel journeys. Determine whether   you’ve implemented omnichannel or single-channel Contacts.
- Omnichannel Journey Solution Workflow Review the solution workflow for creating an omnichannel journey in Marketing Cloud   Engagement using data from Data 360 .
- Stage Your Data in Data 360 Customers commonly implement Marketing Cloud Engagement to create many different   SubscriberKeys (Individuals) that represent the same person. Such SubscriberKeys are often   channel-specific and, as a result, can’t natively execute omnichannel journeys. To build an   omnichannel journey, use Data 360 and build a Unified Individual that represents   a single person consisting of separate Marketing Cloud Engagement channel-specific SubscriberKeys   (Individuals) and contact points.
- Define Match Rules for Identity Resolution and Relate Separate Individuals Let’s review the steps for defining match rules for Identity Resolution and relating   separate Individuals in Data 360 .
- Define Reconciliation Rules to Prioritize Values for the Unified Individual Reconciliation rules specify how to select the best value for a Unified field when that   field can store only one value, such as a person’s first name.
- Create a Calculated Insight to Select the MobilePush SubscriberKey Data 360 has numerous controls to select and activate a channel   contact point. However, for some scenarios, you must create a Calculated Insight to filter or   select a specific channel contact point. For example, Data 360 doesn’t support   activating the Email, SMS, and MobilePush channels together.
- Create an Omnichannel Audience in Data 360 Let’s review the steps that Cumulus takes to create their Omnichannel audience in Data 360 .
- Create a Segment to Qualify the Correct Unified Individuals Cumulus creates a segment that qualifies the Unified Individuals they want to use for   their journey.
- Activate an Audience with Contact Points and Attributes Cumulus activates an audience with contact points and attributes for their   journey.
- Configure Omnichannel Journey Settings in Marketing Cloud Engagement After the scheduled activation, a data extension is added to the Marketing Cloud   Engagement business unit identified in activation. Edit this data extension and update its send   relationship to relate the MobilePush Key attribute to SubscriberKey. As a result, Journey Builder   defaults all orchestration, personalization, and sending lookups based on the value of the   MobilePush Key (representing the MobilePush SubscriberKey selected from the Calculated Insight you   created).
- Update the Send Relationship in the Activated Data Extension Cumulus updates the send relationship in the activated data extension.
- Configure the Journey Entry to Use the Activated Data Extension Audience Next, Cumulus configures its journey entry source.
- Configure Omnichannel Journey Settings Next, Cumulus configures their omnichannel settings. When a journey uses the Omnichannel   Credit Limit Alert data extension Entry Source, Journey Builder defaults all orchestration,   personalization, and sending lookups based on the value of the MobilePush Key. This Key is   represented by the MobilePush SubscriberKey selected from the Calculated Insight. This action   enables you to natively send messages using MobilePush activities.
- Add Consent and Preference Filters to Omnichannel Journeys For the email channel, Marketing Cloud Engagement stores consent at the SubscriberKey   level and not the email address level. By using the MobilePush Key to send an email to the email   address stored in the data extension, Cumulus might have violated their own consent   strategy.
- Omnichannel Considerations and Best Practices There are important aspects and trade-offs to consider before implementing this   solution. This guide is just one example of how to enable an omnichannel experience for your   customers. For example, instead of separate single-channel journeys, users can create seamless   customer experiences by using Data Cloud to orchestrate one journey with all Email, SMS, and   MobilePush activities together.

- Analyze Service Data with Calculated Insights Calculate multidimensional metrics on your data within Data Cloud. You can create     metrics at the profile, segment, and population levels. For example, evaluate performance at the     channel level or use product metrics to understand purchasing and browsing behavior.
- Next Steps with Data Cloud The use cases detailed in this guide give you a glimpse into how you can use Data Cloud     to power your unified Customer 360. When you connect and unify more data sources, the more     useful your unification, insights, and analytics become.

# Implement a Data Foundation in Marketing Cloud Engagement Using Data from Data 360 > Implement a Data Foundation in Marketing Cloud Engagement Using Data from Data 360

You can establish a data foundation by activating data from an external system into
    Marketing Cloud Engagement and linking it to the Engagement Contact Model. You can then refresh
    and reuse this data across Journey Builder for journey decisioning, wait activities, and exits.
    You can also use the data for the content personalization of event-triggered campaigns. This
    solution kit offers a general blueprint on how to set up a data foundation using Data 360 .

This solution kit maximizes both marketer efficiency and end-to-end scale performance while
      reducing the chances of unintentional billing consumption.

Not all campaigns require implementing a data foundation, such as batch sends, transactional
      messages, and journeys that don’t use the Engagement Contact Model for decision splits.

Consider these configuration settings when your campaign does trigger a journey. Use Email as
      the type when creating the Data Extension in Engagement. In Data Cloud, there isn’t an email
      type so the field is text. For the journey to send to contacts that aren’t in Engagement, use
      the Journey Builder setting to use email from any source.

# Manage Data Cloud Data Access Levels for Salesforce Users > Grant Controlled by Parent Access to Data Cloud Data

Relationships between objects are referred to as “parent-child” relationships when one object
    (the parent object) contains values used by another object (the child object).

Granting Controlled by Parent access on a data space lets users view data in a child object as
    long as they have access to view the data in the related parent object. If you grant Controlled
    by Parent access to Data Cloud data, Salesforce users can view Data Cloud data in related lists
    or SOQL query results as long as they have permission to view the record the data is related
    to.

# Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations > Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations

Adding a Data 360 Profile or Data 360 Enterprise Profile license to a Data 360 org
    changes its consumption billing and adds limits for certain features.

All limits associated with Data 360 Profiles licenses apply to the production Data 360 home
      org and its connectioned Data Cloud One companion orgs collectively. Sandbox orgs created from
      the Data 360 home org inherit the home org's limits. Limits apply to the sandbox org and its
      connected companion orgs collectively. To review limits for orgs with Data 360 Profiles
      licenses, see Data 360 Profiles License Base License Limits .

metadata.breadcrumb: Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations > Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations

document:
# Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations > Profiles

The number of profiles included in your Data 360 org cluster is based on how many Data 360
        Profile licenses you purchase. If you exceed your profile entitlement, you’re charged at
        your overage rate.

For production orgs, if identity resolution is active in a data space, the count of
        profiles in each data space is the sum of your known unified profiles, 4% of your anonymous
        profiles, and the total number of records in all DLOs mapped to DMOs categorized as Profile
        that aren’t used by identity resolution.

If identity resolution isn’t active, the billable profile count is the sum of all records
        in all data lake objects (DLOs), regardless of category, mapped to data model objects (DMOs)
        categorized as Profile type, excluding certain DMOs.

For sandbox orgs, the same counting logic applies, but the total number of profiles counted
        toward the limit is 80% of the sum of all profiles in all data spaces on the sandbox
        org.

For a more detailed explanation of how profiles are counted, see Data 360 Profiles License Billable Profiles Calculations .

metadata.breadcrumb: Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations > Profiles

document:
# Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations > Identity Resolution Rulesets

Credits aren’t consumed by the Batch Profile Unification or Data 360 Unification usage
        types when identity resolution runs.

metadata.breadcrumb: Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations > Identity Resolution Rulesets

document:
# Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations > Data Transforms

Credits aren’t consumed by the Batch Data Transforms or Data 360 Prep usage types, but the
        total number of active batch data transforms in your Data 360 org cluster is limited.

For production orgs, the number of batch data transforms counted toward the limit is the sum of all data 
        transforms in all data spaces on the home production org.

For sandbox orgs, the number of batch data transforms counted toward the limit is the sum of all data transforms 
        in all data spaces on the sandbox org.

metadata.breadcrumb: Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations > Data Transforms

document:
# Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations > Calculated Insights

Credits aren’t consumed by the Batch Calculated Insights or Data 360 Prepusage types, but
        the total number of active batch calculated insights in your Data 360 org cluster is
        limited.

For production orgs, the number of batch calculated insights counted toward the limit is the sum of all calculated 
        insights in all data spaces on the home production org.

For sandbox orgs, the number of batch calculated insights counted toward the limit is the sum of all calculated 
        insights in all data spaces on the sandbox org.

metadata.breadcrumb: Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations > Calculated Insights

document:
# Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations > Segmentation

Credits aren’t consumed by the Segmentation or Data 360 Segmentation usage types, but the
        total number of active segments (including standard, waterfall and real-time types) in your
        Data 360 org cluster is limited.

For production orgs, the number of segments counted toward the limit is the sum of all segments in all data spaces 
        on the home production org and all segments in all data space on all connected Data Cloud One Companion orgs.

For sandbox orgs, the number of segments counted toward the limit is the sum of all segments in all data spaces on 
        the sandbox org.

metadata.breadcrumb: Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations > Segmentation

document:
# Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations > All Other Features

Activations: Credits aren’t consumed by the Batch Activation Data 360 Activation
        usage types, but the total number of active batch activations on DMOs in your Data 360 org
        cluster is limited. Streaming DMO activations consume credits.

Data Ingestion: Credits aren’t consumed when data is ingested via an internal data
        pipeline from a Salesforce org or via a batch data connection from an external source.
        Streaming data ingestion consumes credits.

Zero Copy Data Federation: Data federation via live queries and data federation via
        file federation don’t consume the Data Federation or Sharing Rows Accessed usage type. This
        usage type is still consumed by data sharing. Data federation with acceleration doesn’t
        consume the Batch Data Ingestion usage type.

AI Inferences: AI inferences don’t consume the Inferences usage type.

Data transforms, identity resolution, insights, and segments: These features
        continue to consume supplementary usage types listed in their Billing Considerations, such
        as Data Queries and data storage.

All Other Features: All other features continue to consume credits at the regular
        rates as referenced in the Data Services Billable Usage Types for Data 360 and the
        features’ Billing Considerations.

- Data 360 Profiles License Billable Profiles Calculations In orgs with a Data 360 Profiles license, the billable number of profiles is based on whether you have active      Identity Resolution rulesets. You’re billed at your overage rates for additional profiles if the number of billable      profiles exceeds your entitlement.

metadata.breadcrumb: Data 360 Profiles License Billing Considerations > All Other Features

# Data 360 Profiles License Base License Limits > Data 360 Profiles License Base License Limits

Limits in this document represent the base limits of a single Data 360 Profiles or Data 360 
  Enterprise Profiles license. Some limits can be raised by purchasing multiple copies of the license or buying add-on licenses.

metadata.doc_title: Data 360 Profiles License Base License Limits

document:
# Data 360 Profiles License Base License Limits > Data 360 Profile Limits on Data Cloud One Companion Orgs and Sandbox

Orgs

Data Cloud One Org Companion Orgs: Batch calculated insights and segments created on companion orgs are counted 
    toward the Data 360 home org’s limit.

For example, if the home org purchases the base Data 360 Profiles license without any add-ons, it’s limited to 25 batch 
    calculated insights. If the home org has 20 batch calculated insights and the companion org has 5 batch calculated insights, 
    the org cluster has hit its limit of 25 batch calculated insights.

Data 360 Sandboxes: Each sandbox org created from the production Data 360 home org
    inherits the limits of its parent org. Identity resolution rulesets, batch data transforms,
    batch calculated insights, and segments on the Data 360 sandbox org and its connected companion
    orgs are counted toward the Data 360 sandbox org’s limit.

On sandbox orgs, the number of profiles counted toward the profile limit is calculated by
    multiplying the number of profiles by the weight. For example, if a production org has 100
    unified profiles with a weight of 1, then 100 unified profiles times 1 is counted as 100 unified
    profiles (100 x 1 = 100 profiles). A sandbox org’s profiles have a weight of 0.8. Therefore, 100
    profiles on a sandbox are counted as 80 profiles (100 x 0.8 = 80).

metadata.doc_title: Data 360 Profiles License Base License Limits
metadata.section_title: Data 360 Profile Limits on Data Cloud One Companion Orgs and Sandbox

# Data 360 Profiles License Base License Limits > Base License Limits for Data 360 Profiles and Data 360 Enterprise Profiles Licenses

Additional segments can be purchased in blocks of 10 segments.

Deactivated segments aren’t counted toward this limit.

Additional insights can be purchased in blocks of 2 insights.

Streaming insights aren’t included with or limited by this license.

# Data 360 Reportable Resource References > Data 360 Reportable Resource References

Resource references are standard usage tags that let you view your credit consumption by
  the feature that generated the usage. You can build custom Data 360 reports on resource types to
  view, filter, and sort your usage by its source.

Because resource references are organized by feature, usage that is counted against different
    usage types is sometimes bundled together. For example, batch connectors and streaming
    connectors consume credits in different usage types, but are both reported by the same resource
    reference.

After creating a report on a Resource Type, sort by the Resource ID or API Name field to see
    what within the feature generated usage. For example, if you create a report on the
    DataStreamDefinition resource type, sorting by connector API names stored in the Resource ID or
    API Name field lets you see how much each connection contributed to your usage.

metadata.breadcrumb: Data 360 Reportable Resource References > Data 360 Reportable Resource References

# Data Space References in Standard Consumption Tags > Data Space References in Standard Consumption Tags

Filter and group reports about your Data 360 consumption usage by data
    space.

The data space name is captured in the Data Space API field in the TenantUsageAttrDetail data
      lake object (DLO). To use it, build a Data 360 report that breaks down consumption by data
      space by joining the TenantEnrichedUsageEvent and TenantUsageAttrDetail DLOs on Tenant Billing Usage Event Id .

You don’t consume credits when querying or reporting on these DLOs. You can build reports in
      other ways, such as by reporting on the Consumption Insights Extended data model object (DMO)
      or creating a Tableau Next Viz. Some reporting methods can consume credits.

Data space attribution is only available for usage types related to data space aware
      features. on the Data 360 Data Services consumption card, these usage types can be grouped and
      filtered by data space.

- Data Queries
- Unstructured Data Processed
- Data Transforms on data model objects
- Batch Profile Unification
- Segments Processed
- Calculated Insights
- Batch Activations
- Activate DMO - Streaming
- Streaming Actions
- Sub-second Real-Time Events

# Attribute Data Query Costs to Agentforce Sessions and API Requests > Attribute Data Query Costs to Agentforce Sessions and API Requests

The CorrelationIdentifier__c field in Digital Wallet billing
    events connects Data 360 query credit consumption to source processes such as
    the Agentforce session, AI agent, or API call that triggered the query.

When a request triggers a Data 360 query such as an Agentforce agent
      action, a prompt, a report, or a direct API call, an identifier propagates through the query
      pipeline. The identifier is recorded as CorrelationIdentifier__c in the TenantEnrichedUsageEvent data lake object (DLO). You can use this field
      to attribute data query credit consumption to specific agents, sessions, and users.

CorrelationIdentifier__c can be used to attribute costs for the Data
        Queries usage type.

metadata.doc_title: Attribute Data Query Costs to Agentforce Sessions and API Requests
metadata.section_title: Attribute Data Query Costs to Agentforce Sessions and API Requests
metadata.breadcrumb: Attribute Data Query Costs to Agentforce Sessions and API Requests > Attribute Data Query Costs to Agentforce Sessions and API Requests

document:
# Attribute Data Query Costs to Agentforce Sessions and API Requests > Report on Query Costs by Request Origin

To attribute query credit consumption to an Agentforce session or other originating
        request:

- Query the TenantEnrichedUsageEvent DLO and filter on usage type.
          Filter for DataCloud_DataQueries if you're using Data Services
          credits, or for Data360_Queries if your org uses Flex Credits for
          Data 360.
- Group or filter by CorrelationIdentifier__c to isolate consumption
          from specific requests or sessions.
- Join CorrelationIdentifier__c to the corresponding trace ID in your
          Agentforce session data.

You don't consume credits when querying or reporting on the TenantEnrichedUsageEvent DLO directly. Some other reporting methods,
        such as creating a Tableau visualization, can consume credits.

metadata.doc_title: Attribute Data Query Costs to Agentforce Sessions and API Requests

# Billing Impact of Data 360–Powered Features > Billing Impact of Data 360 –Powered Features

Some Salesforce CRM features are powered by Data 360 data. These features impact Data
        Services Credit consumption by increasing usage of associated processes in Data 360 (such
        as querying, storage, processing, and analytics). Before configuring Data 360 -powered
        features, review feature and usage documentation. Contact your account executive to
        understand how features impact Data Services Credit consumption in Data 360 .

After enablement, monitor credit consumption to ensure that the usage is in line with
            your expectations.

Consumption charges aren’t applicable to former Customer Data Platform customers under an
            original contract. Contact your account executive if you have questions about your
            account or consumption charges.

# Data Cloud License Billing and Limits > Data Cloud License Billing and Limits (Part 1)

Adding a Data Cloud license enables Data 360 on a Salesforce org.
    Orgs with this license purchase consumption credits which are consumed by use of Data 360 services.

Depending on when you purchased or renewed your Data Cloud license, your org consumes either
      Data Services credits or Flex Credits for Data 360 services. Review Digital Wallet to
      determine which type of credits apply to you.

metadata.doc_title: Data Cloud License Billing and Limits
metadata.section_title: Data Cloud License Billing and Limits (Part 1)
metadata.breadcrumb: Data Cloud License Billing and Limits > Data Cloud License Billing and Limits (Part 1)

document:
# Data Cloud License Billing and Limits > Data Cloud License Billing and Limits (Part 2)

- Flex Credits Billable Usage Types for Data 360 Usage of certain Data 360 features impacts credit consumption. To monitor your usage in     Flex Credits usage categories, access your org’s Digital Wallet. If your org has a Data 360     Profiles-type license, some usage types aren't consumed. For more information on how usage is     billed, refer to your contract or contact your account executive.
- Data Services Billable Usage Types for Data 360 Usage of certain Data 360 features impacts credit consumption. If you     purchased credits before February 24, 2026, your org consumes Data Services credits for Data 360     services. Orgs purchasing or renewing after February 24, 2026 can have either Data Services or     Flex Credits. To monitor your usage in these Data Services usage categories, access your org’s     Digital Wallet. If your org has a Data 360 Profiles-type license, some usage types aren't     consumed. For more information on how usage is billed, refer to your contract or contact your     account executive.
- Data 360 Limits and Guidelines Guidelines define best practice recommendations to optimize your adoption of Data 360 for best performance. Limits are boundaries beyond which features are     unavailable, performance is throttled, or usage billing charges are applied. Since Data 360 is built to scale, some limits can be adjusted to meet your business     needs. Work with your account executive to find a solution that meets your goals.

metadata.doc_title: Data Cloud License Billing and Limits

# Customer Data Platform License Billing and Limits > Customer Data Platform License Billing and Limits

Customers with this license have access to Data 360 on a Salesforce org. This license
    is no longer available for purchase and can't be renewed. Orgs with this license are billed
    based on the numbers of profiles, engagements, and other records in their orgs. Other features
    have limits. Not all Data 360 features are available on Data 360 orgs with this license.

- Migrate Users from a Customer Data Platform License to a Data Cloud License When you add a Data Cloud license to an org that was previously operating Data 360 under a Customer Data Platform license, the permission sets granted by     the Customer Data Platform license no longer grants access to Data 360 . To     provide users continued access to Data 360 , you must assign the permission     sets associated with the Data Cloud license to your users.
- Customer Data Platform Billable Usage Calculations Previously named Customer Data Platform orgs are billed based on contracted   entitlements. Understanding which usage is included for billing helps you make data management   decisions.
- Customer Data Platform Limits and Guidelines Guidelines define best practice recommendations to optimize the adoption of Data 360 by Customer Data Platform customers for best performance. Limits are     boundaries beyond which features are unavailable, performance is throttled, or usage billing     charges are applied. This article is about the legacy Customer Data Platform license, which is     no longer available for purchase.
